hypothesis: The cone's defect is asymmetric: the left tail is underweight (q05 pinball ratio 1.048 vs EWMA on reconstructed rows) while the right tail is the model's strength. A symmetric Student-t (arms H/F, runs 4 and 6) thickened both tails and overshot the left on the 320-row set. An innovation distribution with a separate left-tail shape (skewed t, or a two-piece t with its own lower-tail degrees of freedom) should lower the q05 ratio on both sets without giving back the q90/q95 gain.

rule: On the holdout (origin=prospective, all h pooled): improved if q05 pinball ratio drops by >= 0.01 vs run 3 (about 7x the 0.0015 Monte-Carlo noise floor measured by run 5) AND mean pinball (model) does not rise by > 0.01; regressed if either q05 ratio rises by > 0.01 or mean pinball rises by > 0.01; otherwise flat.
